key_insight: A systematic review shows that advanced surface engineering—especially multi-principal element, high-entropy, and graded coating systems—can substantially improve metallic component durability by tuning microstructure, adhesion, wear, corrosion, and thermal stability.
engineering_relevance: The findings guide selection of PVD, CVD, thermal spray, electrochemical deposition, and laser cladding routes for aerospace, biomedical, and energy parts where performance under thermal cycling and harsh environments is critical.
method: Compared coating/process families: APS, HVOF, PS-PVD, PVD, CVD, electrochemical deposition, laser cladding
Synthesized processing–structure–property links using characterization and modeling methods
evidence_signal: The review aggregates evidence from more than 90 recent publications and evaluates properties using techniques such as nanoindentation, EIS, pin-on-disk tribometry, XCT, and Raman spectroscopy.
watch_item: A major limitation is the lack of multiscale predictive models and scalable green manufacturing routes, which can slow translation to reliable industrial and clinical deployment.
paper_title: Surface Engineering and Coating Technologies: A Systematic Review was Conducted on the Use of Metallic Components
